properties.line: Central Pacific: San Joaquin Valley Line
properties.speed_source: estimated/blended: a fast, flat, arrow-straight Central Valley alignment, rising from 1870s local-train speeds to the streamlined Daylight-era expresses of the mid-20th century; unsourced

segments.note: Sacramento-Stockton opened Aug 11 1869, shortly after the Central Pacific finished the transcontinental line at Promontory. Late that year the CP began pushing south from Lathrop (just below Stockton) down the flat, arrow-straight San Joaquin Valley: Lathrop-Modesto opened Nov 8 1870, Modesto-Merced Jan 15 1872, and Merced-Fresno May 28 1872, completing the route shown here (the CP's own construction continued another 53 miles south to Goshen Junction before Southern Pacific took over building further south). Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: Leased to the Southern Pacific Company on April 1 1885 (formally merged into SP in 1959, though the CP corporate identity lingered on paper for decades). Valley trains of this era included the overnight Owl. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

segments.note: By the 1940s the line's flagship was the streamlined San Joaquin Daylight (Oakland/San Francisco-Fresno-Bakersfield, connecting to Los Angeles), running alongside the Sacramento Daylight and the West Coast. The San Joaquin Daylight made its last run April 30 1971, the day before Amtrak began -- Amtrak did not continue it, and when Amtrak's own San Joaquins service launched in 1974 it ran on the parallel Santa Fe line through the valley rather than this route, which has carried freight only ever since (Southern Pacific, then Union Pacific from the 1996 SP-UP merger, as today's UP Fresno Subdivision).
